sentences.zh: 顯德二年春正月辛未朔，帝不受朝賀。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiande, spring, on the first day of the first month (xinwei, the new moon), the Emperor did not receive court congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Xiande 2, on the new-moon day xinwei of the first month, the emperor declined the usual New Year court congratulations.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，詔：「在朝文班，各舉堪為令錄者一人，雖姻族近親，亦無妨嫌。

translations.literal: On xinmao, an edict: "Among the civil officials at court, each shall recommend one person fit to serve as magistrate or recorder; even close kin by marriage shall not be barred."
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao an edict ordered each civil official at court to nominate one person qualified to be a county magistrate or clerk, without disqualifying even close relatives by marriage.

sentences.zh: 授官之日，各署舉主姓名，若在官貪濁不任、懦弱不理，並量事狀重輕，連坐舉主。

translations.literal: On the day offices are conferred, each shall record the recommender's name; if the appointee in office is corrupt and incompetent or timid and neglectful, according to the seriousness of the matter the recommender shall be punished in connection.
translations.idiomatic: At appointment each record was to name the sponsor; if an officeholder proved corrupt, incompetent, or timid and neglectful in office, the sponsor would share punishment according to the gravity of the case.

sentences.zh: 」乙未，詔：「應逃戶莊田，並許人請射承佃，供納稅租：如三周年內本戶來歸者，其莊田不計荒熟，並交還一半；

translations.literal: " On yiwei, an edict: "As to estate fields of absconding households, all are permitted to others to bid and lease for cultivation, supplying tax rent: if within three full years the original household returns, their estate fields, regardless of waste or ripeness, shall together be returned half;
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei another edict allowed others to bid for and farm fields left by fleeing households while paying taxes; if the original household returned within three years, half the land—whether fallow or cultivated—was to be restored to them;

sentences.zh: 五周年內歸業者，三分交還一分；

translations.literal: Those returning to production within five years, of three parts return one part;
translations.idiomatic: those who returned within five years received one-third back;

sentences.zh: 如五周年外歸業者，其莊田除本戶墳塋外，不在交付之限。

translations.literal: if returning to production after five years, their estate fields, except the original household's graves, are not within the limit of delivery.
translations.idiomatic: after five years only the family grave plots were exempt from return to the original household.

sentences.zh: 其近北地諸州，應有陷蕃人戶，自蕃界來歸業者：五周年內來者，三分交還二分；

translations.literal: As to the various prefectures of the near-northern region, there should be households fallen among the Fan—those returning to production from the Fan border: within five years, of three return two;
translations.idiomatic: In northern border prefectures, for households that had fallen to the Khitans and returned from enemy territory: within five years two-thirds were returned;

sentences.zh: 十周年內來者，交還一半；

translations.literal: within ten years, return half;
translations.idiomatic: within ten years, half;

sentences.zh: 十五周年來者，三分交還一分；

translations.literal: at fifteen years, of three return one;
translations.idiomatic: at fifteen years, one-third;

sentences.zh: 十五周年外來者，不在交還之限。」

translations.literal: those coming after fifteen years are not within the limit of return."
translations.idiomatic: beyond fifteen years nothing was returned.

sentences.zh: 二月戊申，遣使赴西京，賜太子太師致仕侯益、白文珂、宋彥筠等茶藥錢帛各有差，仍降詔存問。

translations.literal: On wushen in the second month, envoys were sent to the Western Capital to bestow tea, medicines, money, and silks on the retired Grand Preceptor Hou Yi, Bai Wenke, Song Yanjun, and others, each in differing amounts, and an edict of inquiry was also issued.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen in the second month the court sent envoys to Luoyang with tea, medicines, cash, and silks for the retired Grand Preceptor Hou Yi, Bai Wenke, Song Yanjun, and others in graded amounts, along with an edict of gracious inquiry.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，詔曰：

translations.literal: On renxu, an edict stated:
translations.idiomatic: On renxu the emperor promulgated an edict:

sentences.zh: 善操理者不能有全功，善處身者不能無過失。

translations.literal: Those skilled in governance cannot achieve complete success; those skilled in self-conduct cannot be without faults.
translations.idiomatic: Even the ablest administrators cannot achieve flawless success, and even the most prudent men cannot avoid all error.

sentences.zh: 雖堯、舜、禹、湯之上聖，文、武、成康之至明，尚猶思逆耳之言，求苦口之藥，何況後人之不逮哉！

translations.literal: Although Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang were supreme sages, and Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang were the utmost in clarity, they still sought words that grated on the ear and medicines bitter to the mouth—how much more those of later times who do not reach them!
translations.idiomatic: Though Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang were supreme sages, and King Wen, King Wu, King Cheng, and King Kang models of enlightened rule, they still welcomed harsh counsel and bitter remedies—how much more must lesser rulers do so!

sentences.zh: 朕承先帝之靈，居至尊之位，涉道猶淺，經事未深，常懼昏蒙，不克負荷。

translations.literal: We have received the spirit of the former emperor and occupy the position of supreme honor; our acquaintance with the Way is still shallow and our experience in affairs not yet deep—we constantly fear dullness and inability to bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: Having inherited the throne through my predecessor's mandate, I am still shallow in learning and inexperienced in government, and I constantly fear that my dullness will prove unequal to the burden.

sentences.zh: 自臨宸極，已過周星，至於刑政取舍之間，國家措置之事，豈能盡是，須有未周，朕猶自知，人豈不察。

translations.literal: Since assuming the imperial throne, more than a year has passed; as to choices in punishment and government and measures for the state, how could all be correct—there must be points not yet thorough; We ourselves know this—would others not perceive it?
translations.idiomatic: Since I took the throne more than a year has passed; in criminal law, policy, and national measures there must be gaps I have not yet closed—I know this myself, and surely others see it too.

sentences.zh: 而在位者未有一人指朕躬之過失，食祿者曾無一言論時政之是非，豈朕之寡昧不足與言邪？

translations.literal: Yet among those in office not one has pointed out faults in Our person; among those receiving stipends not one word on whether current policy is right or wrong—is it that Our dullness is unworthy of speech?
translations.idiomatic: Yet not one official in office has pointed out my personal failings, and not one salaried officer has judged whether current policy is right or wrong—is it that I am too dull to be addressed?

sentences.zh: 豈人之循默未肯盡心邪？

translations.literal: Is it that men follow silence and are unwilling to give their full hearts?
translations.idiomatic: Or that men follow custom in silence and will not speak wholeheartedly?

sentences.zh: 豈左右前後有所畏忌邪？

translations.literal: Is it that those left and right, before and behind, have something to fear?
translations.idiomatic: Or that those around me are restrained by fear?

sentences.zh: 豈高卑疏近自生間別邪？

translations.literal: Is it that high and low, distant and near, spontaneously create distinctions?
translations.idiomatic: Or that rank and distance create needless barriers between us?

sentences.zh: 古人云：「君子大言受大祿，小言受小祿。

translations.literal: The ancients said: "The gentleman who speaks greatly receives great emolument; he who speaks little receives little emolument."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, "A gentleman who speaks boldly deserves great reward; one who speaks modestly, a lesser reward."

sentences.zh: 」又云：「官箴王闕。

translations.literal: " Again it is said: "Officials admonish the king's shortcomings."
translations.idiomatic: They also said, "Officers are to correct the ruler's faults."

sentences.zh: 」則是士大夫之有祿位，無不言之人。

translations.literal: " Then scholars and officials who hold stipends are people who do not remain silent.
translations.idiomatic: Thus any scholar-official who draws a salary ought to speak up.

sentences.zh: 然則為人上者，不能感其心而致其言，此朕之過也。

translations.literal: Yet for one above, unable to move their hearts and elicit their words—this is Our fault.
translations.idiomatic: If I as sovereign have failed to win their hearts and draw out their counsel, the fault is mine.

sentences.zh: 得不求骨鯁之辭，詢正直之議，共申裨益，庶洽治平。

translations.literal: We must seek words like bones in the throat and inquire into upright criticism, together extending benefit—may governance reach peace.
translations.idiomatic: I must therefore seek blunt counsel and honest criticism so that together we may improve governance and bring the realm to peace.

sentences.zh: 朕於卿大夫才不能盡知，面不能盡識，若不采其言而觀其行，審其意而察其忠，則何以見器量之深淺，知任用之當否？

translations.literal: We cannot fully know the talents of you ministers and great officers, nor fully recognize faces; if We do not take their words and observe their conduct, examine their intent and discern their loyalty, how can We see the depth of their capacity and know whether appointment is fitting?
translations.idiomatic: I cannot know every minister's full talent nor recognize every face; unless I heed your words, watch your conduct, and weigh your loyalty, how can I judge your capacity or whether you are rightly placed?

sentences.zh: 若言之不入，罪實在予；

translations.literal: If words do not enter, the fault is truly in Us;
translations.idiomatic: If your words do not reach me, the fault is truly mine;

sentences.zh: 茍求之不言，咎將誰執！

translations.literal: if seeking them you do not speak, upon whom will the blame fall!
translations.idiomatic: but if I ask and you still withhold speech, upon whom will blame fall?

sentences.zh: 應內外文武臣僚，今後或有所見所聞，並許上章論諫。

translations.literal: All civil and military officials within and without, from now on if they have something seen or heard, are permitted to memorialize and remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth all civil and military officials at court and in the provinces who observe or hear anything may submit memorials of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 若朕躬之有闕失，得以盡言；

translations.literal: If there are faults in Our person, they may speak fully;
translations.idiomatic: If I have personal failings, you may state them fully;

sentences.zh: 時政之有瑕疵，勿宜有隱。

translations.literal: if there are flaws in current policy, they should not be concealed.
translations.idiomatic: if current policy is flawed, you must not conceal it.

sentences.zh: 方求名實，豈尚虛華，茍或素不工文，但可直書其事。

translations.literal: We seek name and reality—how could We esteem empty show; if one is ordinarily not skilled in letters, one may simply write the matter plainly.
translations.idiomatic: I seek substance, not show; if you are no stylist, write plainly what you mean.

sentences.zh: 辭有謬誤者，固當舍短，言涉傷忤者，必與留中，所冀盡情，免至多慮。

translations.literal: Where words have errors, We shall of course overlook the shortcoming; where words touch and give offense, We shall certainly retain them at court—the hope is full expression, free from excessive worry.
translations.idiomatic: Errors in wording I will overlook; even offensive speech I will keep and consider, so that you may speak freely without undue fear.

sentences.zh: 諸有司局公事者，各宜舉職，事有不便者，革之可也，理有可行者，舉之可也，勿務因循，漸成訛謬。

translations.literal: Those in charge of bureau affairs in the various offices should each perform duty; where affairs are inconvenient, they may be reformed; where principle permits action, it may be raised—do not cling to routine until errors gradually accumulate.
translations.idiomatic: Each bureau should perform its duties: reform what is awkward, advance what is sound, and do not cling to routine until mistakes pile up.

sentences.zh: 臣僚有出使在外回者，茍或知黎庶之利病，聞官吏之優劣，當具敷奏，以廣聽聞。

translations.literal: If officials returning from missions abroad know the people's ills and benefits or hear of officials' merits and defects, they should memorialize in detail to broaden Our hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Officials returning from missions abroad should report in full any knowledge of the people's hardships or of officials' merits and faults.

sentences.zh: 班行職位之中，遷除改轉之際，即當考陳力之輕重，較言事之否臧，奉公切直者當議甄升，臨事蓄縮者須期抑退。

translations.literal: Among ranks and offices, at the time of promotion and transfer, one should assess the weight of their exertion and compare whether their speech was right or wrong—those devoted and upright in public service should be considered for advancement; those who shrink from affairs should expect demotion.
translations.idiomatic: At promotion time assess each man's effort and the truth of his counsel: reward the devoted and forthright, and expect to demote those who shrink from duty.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士、兩省官職居侍從，乃論思諫諍之司；

translations.literal: Hanlin academicians and officials of the two departments who attend close to the throne are the offices for reflection and remonstrance;
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academicians and the two departments' attendants are charged with reflection and remonstrance;

sentences.zh: 御史臺官任處憲綱，是擊搏糾彈之地。

translations.literal: Censorate officials bear the constitutional net—they are the place for striking and impeaching.
translations.idiomatic: censorate officers hold the constitutional charge and are to investigate and impeach.

sentences.zh: 論其職分，尤異群臣，如逐任官內，所獻替啟發彈舉者，至月限滿合遷轉時，宜令中書門下先奏取進止。

translations.literal: Considering their duties, they differ especially from the multitude of officials; if within successive terms in office they present replacements, enlightenments, or impeachments, when the monthly term is full and transfer is due, the Secretariat and Chancellery should first memorialize for Our decision.
translations.idiomatic: Their role is distinct from other officials: when their term ends, if they have offered constructive memorials or impeachments, the Secretariat and Chancellery should first report to me before their transfer.

sentences.zh: 三月辛未，以李晏口為靜安軍，其軍南距冀州百里，北距深州三十里，夾胡盧河為壘。

translations.literal: On xinwei in the third month, Li Yankou was made Jing'an Army; the army was a hundred li south of Jizhou and thirty li north of Shenzhou, with fortifications straddling the Hulu River.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei in the third month Li Yankou was established as Jing'an Army, positioned a hundred li south of Jizhou and thirty li north of Shenzhou with fortifications along the Hulu River.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：浚胡盧河在正月，至三月始建軍額。）〉

translations.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: The dredging of the Hulu River was in the first month; the army designation was not created until the third month.)]
translations.idiomatic: (Zizhi Tongjian: The dredging of the Hulu River was in the first month; the army designation was not created until the third month.)]

sentences.zh: 先是，貝、冀之境密邇戎疆，居常敵騎涉河而南，馳突往來洞無阻礙，北鄙之地民不安居。

translations.literal: Earlier, the border between Bei and Ji prefectures closely adjoined the Rong frontier; enemy cavalry often crossed the river southward and raided back and forth with no obstruction; the people of the northern marches could not dwell in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the Bei-Ji border lay against the steppe, and Khitan horsemen often crossed the river to raid at will, so northern villagers lived in constant insecurity.

sentences.zh: 帝乃按圖定策，遣許州節度使王彥超、曹州節度使韓通等領兵他徙，築壘於李晏口，以兵戍守，功未畢，契丹眾尋至，彥超等擊退之。

translations.literal: The Emperor then consulted maps and fixed strategy, dispatching Xuzhou Military Commissioner Wang Yanchao, Caozhou Military Commissioner Han Tong, and others to lead troops elsewhere and build fortifications at Li Yankou with garrison troops; before the work was finished, Khitan forces soon arrived and Yanchao and others repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then planned from maps and sent Wang Yanchao of Xu and Han Tong of Cao to relocate troops and build fortifications at Li Yankou; before the works were finished Khitan forces arrived and were beaten back.

sentences.zh: 及壘成，頗扼要害，自是敵騎雖至，不敢涉河，邊民稍得耕牧焉。

translations.literal: When the fortifications were complete, they largely choked the strategic points; from then on though enemy cavalry came, they did not dare cross the river, and border people gradually obtained plowing and herding.
translations.idiomatic: Once the works were complete they held the key points; thereafter enemy horsemen came but dared not cross, and border folk gradually resumed farming and herding.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，尚書禮部貢院進新及第進士李覃等一十六人所試詩賦、文論、策文等。

translations.literal: On renchen, the Ministry of Rites examination hall presented the newly passed jinshi Li Tan and fifteen others with their trial poems, essays, discourses, and policy answers.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the Ministry of Rites presented the sixteen newly passed candidates, including Li Tan, with their examination compositions.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「國家設貢舉之司，求英俊之士，務詢文行，方中科名。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "The state establishes the examination service to seek talented men, requiring inquiry into culture and conduct before bestowing rank."
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "The state holds examinations to find able men of both learning and character before granting degrees."

sentences.zh: 比聞近年以來，多有濫進，或以年勞而得第，或因媒勢以出身。

translations.literal: "We have heard that in recent years many have passed improperly—some gaining degrees through seniority, some entering office through patronage."
translations.idiomatic: We hear that in recent years many unworthy men have passed, some by seniority and some by connections.

sentences.zh: 今歲所放舉人，試令看驗，果見紕繆，須至去留。

translations.literal: "This year's candidates, when ordered examined, were indeed found flawed and must be kept or dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: This year's candidates were re-examined and found deficient; retention or dismissal is required.

sentences.zh: 其李覃、何嚴、楊徽之、趙鄰幾等四人，宜放及第。

translations.literal: Li Tan, He Yan, Yang Huizhi, Zhao Linji, and four others should be granted passage.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tan, He Yan, Yang Huizhi, and Zhao Linji—the four of them—are to receive degrees.

sentences.zh: 其嚴說、武允成、王汾、閭邱舜卿、任惟吉、周度、張慎徽、王翥、馬文、劉選、程浩然、李震等一十二人，藝學未精，並宜勾落，且令苦學，以俟再來。

translations.literal: Yan Shuo, Wu Yuncheng, Wang Fen, Lüqiu Shunqing, Ren Weiji, Zhou Du, Zhang Shenhui, Wang Zhu, Ma Wen, Liu Xuan, Cheng Haoran, Li Zhen, and twelve others—their arts and learning not yet refined—should all be struck from the list and ordered to study hard, awaiting another attempt.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shuo, Wu Yuncheng, Wang Fen, Lüqiu Shunqing, Ren Weiji, Zhou Du, Zhang Shenhui, Wang Zhu, Ma Wen, Liu Xuan, Cheng Haoran, Li Zhen, and twelve others lacked sufficient skill and are to be struck from the rolls and told to study hard for a future attempt.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎劉溫叟失於選士，頗屬因循，據其過尤，合行譴謫，尚視寬恕，特與矜容，劉溫叟放罪，其將來貢舉公事，仍令所司別具條理以聞。」

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Liu Wensou failed in selecting scholars and was quite perfunctory; according to his faults, dismissal was appropriate, yet viewing lenience, special forbearance was granted—Liu Wensou was pardoned; future examination affairs are still to be separately regulated and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Liu Wensou had been negligent in selection and deserved punishment, but he was pardoned; future examination rules are to be reported separately.

sentences.zh: 夏四月庚戌，以內客省使李彥頵為延州留後。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on gengxu, Interior Client Commissioner Li Yanbin was made acting prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu in the fourth month Li Yanbin, commissioner of the Interior Client Service, was made acting prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，詔：「應自外新除御史，未經朝謝，行過州府，不得受館驛供給及所在公禮。

translations.literal: On xinhai, an edict: "Newly appointed censors from outside who have not yet attended court audience, when passing through prefectures, must not receive lodge supplies from post stations or local public gifts."
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai an edict forbade newly appointed censors who had not yet presented themselves at court from accepting post-station hospitality or local gifts while traveling through prefectures.

sentences.zh: 」乙卯，詔於京城四面別築羅城，期以來春興役。

translations.literal: " On yimao, an edict to build separate outer walls on all four sides of the capital, with labor to begin the coming spring.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the court ordered outer walls built on all four sides of the capital, with work to begin the following spring.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以翰林學士、給事中竇儀為禮部侍郎，依前充職；

translations.literal: On wuwu, Hanlin Academician and Attendant-in-Waiting Dou Yi was made Vice Minister of Rites while continuing in his former post;
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Dou Yi, Hanlin academician and attendant-in-waiting, was made vice minister of rites while retaining his former duties;

sentences.zh: 以禮部侍郎劉溫叟為太子詹事。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Liu Wensou was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wensou was transferred to grand mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以翰林學士、中書舍人楊昭儉為御史中丞。

translations.literal: On guihai, Hanlin Academician and Secretariat Drafter Yang Zhaojian was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Yang Zhaojian, Hanlin academician and drafter, was made censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 是月，詔翰林學士承旨徐臺符已下二十餘人，各撰《為君難為臣不易論》、《平邊策》各一首，帝親覽之。

translations.literal: This month, an edict ordered Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance Xu Taifu and more than twenty others each to compose one "On the Difficulty of Being Ruler and Subject" and one "Strategy for Pacifying the Border," which the Emperor personally reviewed.
translations.idiomatic: That month the emperor ordered Xu Taifu, Hanlin academician-in-attendance, and more than twenty colleagues each to write an essay on the difficulty of being ruler and subject and a border-pacification strategy, which he read personally.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·陶蒨傳》：世宗謂宰相曰：「朕觀歷代君臣治平之道，誠為不易，又念唐、晉失德之後，亂臣黠將，僭竊者多。

translations.literal: (《宋史·陶蒨傳》:世宗謂宰相曰：「朕觀歷代君臣治平之道，誠為不易，又念唐、晉失德之後，亂臣黠將，僭竊者多。
translations.idiomatic: (Song Shi, biography of Tao Qian: The Emperor told the chief ministers, "I observe that the way of rulers and subjects to order and peace in every age is truly not easy; moreover, after the moral failures of Tang and Jin, rebellious ministers and cunning generals who usurped were many."

sentences.zh: 今中原甫定，吳、蜀、幽、并尚未平附，聲教未能遠被，宣令近臣各為論策，宜導經濟之略。

translations.literal: Now the Central Plain has just been settled; Wu, Shu, You, and Bing are not yet pacified and submitted; our transforming influence cannot yet reach far—it is fitting to order the close ministers each to compose policy essays and guide strategies of statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Plain has just been settled; Wu, Shu, You, and Bing are not yet pacified, and our civilizing influence has not reached far—order the close ministers each to compose policy essays that set forth strategies of statecraft.

sentences.zh: 」乃命承旨徐臺符已下二十餘人，各撰《為君難為臣不易論》、《平邊策》以進。

translations.literal: 乃命承旨徐臺符已下二十餘人，各撰《為君難為臣不易論》、《平邊策》以進。
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Xu Taifu, academician-in-attendance, and more than twenty others each to submit "On the Difficulty of Being Ruler and Subject" and "Strategy for Pacifying the Border."

sentences.zh: 其略率以修文德、來遠人為意，惟蒨與竇儀、楊昭儉、王樸以封疆密邇江、淮，當用師取之。

translations.literal: Their summaries mostly took cultivating civil virtue and drawing distant people as the intent; only Qian, Dou Yi, Yang Zhaojian, and Wang Pu, because the frontier closely adjoins the Yangzi and Huai, held that troops should be used to take it.
translations.idiomatic: Most summaries urged cultivating civil virtue and winning distant peoples; only Tao Qian, Dou Yi, Yang Zhaojian, and Wang Pu argued that with the frontier pressing close to the Yangzi and Huai, troops should be used to take it.

sentences.zh: 世宗自克高平，常訓兵講武，思混一天下，及覽其策，欣然聽納，由是平南之意益堅矣。）〉

translations.literal: Since conquering Gaoping the Emperor had constantly drilled troops and studied war, thinking to unite all under Heaven; when he read these strategies he gladly accepted them, and his resolve to pacify the south grew firmer.)]
translations.idiomatic: Since conquering Gaoping the Emperor had constantly drilled troops and studied war, thinking to unite all under Heaven; when he read these strategies he gladly accepted them, and his resolve to pacify the south grew firmer.)]

sentences.zh: 五月辛未，回鶻遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: On xinwei in the fifth month, the Uighurs sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei in the fifth month Uighur envoys presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔節度使王景上言：「奉詔攻收秦、鳳二州，已於今月一日領軍由大散關路進軍次。

translations.literal: Fengxiang Military Commissioner Wang Jing memorialized: "Obeying the edict to attack and recover Qin and Feng prefectures, on the first of this month I have led the army by the Dasanguan route and advanced to camp."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing, military commissioner of Fengxiang, reported that by imperial order he had marched on the first of the month through Dasanguan toward Qin and Feng.

sentences.zh: 」先是，晉末契丹入晉，秦州節度使何建以秦、成、階三州入蜀，蜀人又取鳳州。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the end of Jin the Khitans entered Jin; Qinzhou Military Commissioner He Jian surrendered Qin, Cheng, and Jie prefectures to Shu, and the Shu people also took Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Later Jin the Khitans invaded; He Jian, military commissioner of Qin, had surrendered Qin, Cheng, and Jie to Shu, and Shu also seized Feng.

sentences.zh: 至是，秦、鳳人戶怨蜀之苛政，相次詣闕，乞舉兵收復舊地，乃詔景與宣徽南院使向訓率師赴焉。

translations.literal: At this time the people of Qin and Feng resented Shu's harsh government and came in succession to the court begging that troops be raised to recover their old lands; an edict then ordered Jing and Xuanhui Southern Court Commissioner Xiang Xun to lead armies there.
translations.idiomatic: Now the people of Qin and Feng, resenting Shu's harsh rule, petitioned the court to recover their territory, and Jing and Xiang Xun of the Southern Court were ordered to lead the campaign.

sentences.zh: （《東都事略·王溥傳》：世宗將討秦、鳳，溥薦向拱，遂平之。

translations.literal: (《東都事略·王溥傳》:世宗將討秦、鳳，溥薦向拱，遂平之。
translations.idiomatic: (Eastern Capital Epitome, biography of Wang Pu: When the Emperor was about to campaign against Qin and Feng, Pu recommended Xiang Gong, and the region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 世宗因宴酌卮酒賜之，曰：「成吾邊功，卿擇帥之力也。」）〉

translations.literal: At a banquet the Emperor poured a cup of wine for him and said, "You achieved our border success by choosing the right commander.")]
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet the Emperor poured a cup of wine for him and said, "You achieved our border success by choosing the right commander.")]

sentences.zh: 甲戌，詔曰：

translations.literal: On jiaxu, an edict stated:
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu a major edict on Buddhism began:

sentences.zh: 釋氏貞宗，聖人妙道，助世勸善，其利甚優。

translations.literal: The orthodox teaching of the Buddha is the subtle Way of the sage, aiding the age and encouraging goodness—its benefit is very great.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism is the sage's subtle way, aiding the age and encouraging goodness, and its benefit is great.

sentences.zh: 前代以來，累有條貫，近年已降，頗紊規繩。

translations.literal: From former ages there have been successive regulations; in recent years regulations have been quite disordered.
translations.idiomatic: Former dynasties issued regulations, but in recent years rules have fallen into disorder.

sentences.zh: 近覽諸州奏聞，繼有緇徒犯法，蓋無科禁，遂至尤違，私度僧尼，日增猥雜，創修寺院，漸至繁多，鄉村之中其弊轉甚。

translations.literal: Recently reviewing memorials from the prefectures, there have been successive cases of monks and nuns breaking the law—because there were no prohibitions they reached extreme violation: privately ordaining monks and nuns, daily increasing in vulgar profusion, creating and repairing monasteries gradually becoming numerous—the abuses in villages and hamlets grow worse.
translations.idiomatic: Recent reports show monks and nuns breaking the law because rules were not enforced: private ordinations multiply, new monasteries proliferate, and abuses in the countryside worsen.

sentences.zh: 漏網背軍之輩，茍剃削以逃刑；

translations.literal: Those who evaded the net and deserted the army, if shaven they escaped punishment;
translations.idiomatic: Deserters shave their heads to escape military punishment;

sentences.zh: 行奸為盜之徒，托住持而隱惡。

translations.literal: those who practiced wickedness and theft relied on abbotship to hide evil.
translations.idiomatic: criminals take monastic residence to hide their crimes.

sentences.zh: 將隆教法，須辨否臧，宜舉舊章，用革前弊。

translations.literal: To exalt the teaching of the law, right and wrong must be distinguished—old regulations should be raised to reform former abuses.
translations.idiomatic: To restore the teaching, right and wrong must be distinguished and old regulations revived to end these abuses.

sentences.zh: 諸道府州縣鎮村坊，應有敕額寺院，一切仍舊，其無敕額者，並仰停廢，所有功德佛像及僧尼，並騰並於合留寺院內安置。

translations.literal: In all circuits, prefectures, counties, towns, villages, and wards, monasteries with imperial patent should all remain as before; those without patent shall be abolished; all merit statues of Buddha and monks and nuns shall be gathered into monasteries that are to remain.
translations.idiomatic: Monasteries with imperial charters remain; those without are abolished, and their images and clergy consolidated into permitted monasteries.

sentences.zh: 天下諸縣城郭內，若無敕額寺院，只於合停廢寺院內，選功德屋宇最多者，或寺院僧尼各留一所，若無尼住，只留僧寺院一所。

translations.literal: Within all county seats in the realm, if there is no patented monastery, only in abolished monasteries select the one with the most merit halls, or among monasteries leave one for monks and nuns each; if no nuns reside, leave only one monks' monastery.
translations.idiomatic: In county seats without a chartered monastery, one abolished site with the most temple buildings may be kept, or one each for monks and nuns where both exist.

sentences.zh: 諸軍鎮坊郭及二百戶已上者，亦依諸縣例指揮。

translations.literal: Military garrisons, market towns, and places with two hundred households or more shall also follow the county precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison towns and settlements of two hundred households or more follow the same rule.

sentences.zh: 如邊遠州郡無敕額寺院處，於停廢寺院內僧尼各留兩所。

translations.literal: In remote border prefectures without patented monasteries, among abolished monasteries leave two each for monks and nuns.
translations.idiomatic: Remote border counties without charters may keep two monasteries each for monks and nuns from abolished sites.

sentences.zh: 今後並不得創造寺院蘭若。

translations.literal: From now on creating monasteries and shrines is not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: New monasteries and shrines are forbidden thereafter.

sentences.zh: 王公戚裏諸道節刺已下，今後不得奏請創造寺院及請開置戒壇。

translations.literal: Princes, imperial kin, circuit commissioners, and prefects and below may not hereafter memorialize to create monasteries or request opening ordination platforms.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, imperial kin, commissioners, and prefects may no longer petition to build monasteries or open ordination platforms.

sentences.zh: 男子女子如有誌願出家者，並取父母、祖父母處分，已孤者取同居伯叔兄處分，候聽許方得出家。

translations.literal: Men and women who wish to leave household life must obtain disposition from parents and grandparents; if orphaned, from co-resident uncles, elder brothers, or cousins—only after permission may they leave household life.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone wishing to become a monk or nun needs written consent from parents or grandparents, or from senior kin if orphaned.

sentences.zh: 男年十五已上，念得經文一百紙，或讀得經文五百紙，女年十三已上，念得經文七十紙，或讀得經文三百紙者，經本府陳狀乞剃頭，委錄事參軍本判官試驗經文。

translations.literal: Males fifteen and above who can recite one hundred sheets of scripture or read five hundred sheets, females thirteen and above who can recite seventy sheets or read three hundred sheets, after memorializing to the prefecture requesting tonsure, shall be tested on scripture by the recorder and judge.
translations.idiomatic: Boys fifteen or older must recite one hundred scrolls or read five hundred; girls thirteen or older, seventy or three hundred; then the prefecture tests them before tonsure.

sentences.zh: 其未剃頭間，須留發髻，如有私剃頭者，卻勒還俗，其本師主決重杖勒還俗，仍配役三年。

translations.literal: Before tonsure the topknot must remain; if privately shaven, they are compelled to return to lay life; the master is beaten severely, compelled to return to lay life, and assigned corvée for three years.
translations.idiomatic: The topknot must remain until lawful tonsure; private shaving forces lay status on novice and master, with three years' corvée for the master.

sentences.zh: 兩京、大名府、京兆府、青州各處置戒壇，候受戒時，兩京委祠部差官引試，其大名府等三處，只委本判官錄事參軍引試。

translations.literal: The two capitals, Damingfu, Jingzhaofu, and Qingzhou each shall have ordination platforms; when receiving precepts, the two capitals shall have the Ministry of Rites dispatch officials to conduct trials; at Damingfu and the other three places only the judge and recorder shall conduct trials.
translations.idiomatic: Ordination platforms exist at the two capitals, Daming, Chang'an, and Qingzhou; capital ordinations are tested by Ministry of Rites officials, the others by local judges.

sentences.zh: 如有私受戒者，其本人、師主、臨壇三綱、知事僧尼，並同私剃頭例科罪。

translations.literal: If precepts are privately received, the person himself, master, the three ranks of the platform, and managing monks and nuns shall all be punished like private tonsure.
translations.idiomatic: Private ordination punishes the candidate, master, platform officers, and managing monks alike.

sentences.zh: 應合剃頭受戒人等，逐處聞奏，候敕下，委祠部給付憑由，方得剃頭受戒。

translations.literal: Those fit for tonsure and receiving precepts in each place shall report; after the edict arrives, the Ministry of Rites shall issue credentials—only then may they be shaven and receive precepts.
translations.idiomatic: Qualified candidates must be reported and receive Ministry credentials before tonsure and precepts.

sentences.zh: 應男女有父母、祖父母在，別無兒息侍養，不聽出家。

translations.literal: Men and women who have parents or grandparents living and no other children to serve them may not leave household life.
translations.idiomatic: Those with living parents or grandparents and no other children to support them may not become monks or nuns.

sentences.zh: 曾有罪犯，遭官司刑責之人，及棄背父母、逃亡奴婢、奸人細作、惡逆徒黨、山林亡命、未獲賊徒、負罪潛竄人等，並不得出家剃頭。

translations.literal: Those who had crimes and suffered official punishment, deserters who abandoned parents, fugitive slaves, spies, wicked conspirators, mountain outlaws, uncaptured bandits, and those guilty who lurk in hiding may not be shaven and leave household life.
translations.idiomatic: Criminals, deserters, fugitive slaves, spies, conspirators, outlaws, bandits, and fugitives may not be ordained.

sentences.zh: 如有寺院輒容受者，其本人及師主、三綱、知事僧尼、鄰房同住僧，並仰收捉禁勘，申奏取裁。

translations.literal: If any monastery rashly accepts them, the person himself and master, the three ranks, managing monks and nuns, and neighboring resident monks shall all be seized, detained, investigated, and memorialized for decision.
translations.idiomatic: Monasteries that harbor them shall have all involved clergy seized and reported for imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 僧尼俗士，自前多有舍身、燒臂、煉指、釘截手足、帶鈴掛燈、諸般毀壞身體、戲弄道具、符禁左道、妄稱變現還魂坐化、聖水聖燈妖幻之類，皆是聚眾眩惑流俗，今後一切止絕。

translations.literal: Monks, nuns, and lay people have in the past often offered their bodies, burned arms, refined fingers, nailed and cut hands and feet, hung bells and lamps, all sorts of destroying the body, playing with implements, talismans and left-hand ways, falsely claiming transformations, returning souls, sitting and transforming, holy water and holy lamps and demon illusions—these all gather crowds to dazzle the vulgar; from now on all are stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Self-mutilation, fire offerings, talismans, false miracles, and similar crowd-deceiving practices are banned entirely.

sentences.zh: 如有此色人，仰所在嚴斷，遞配邊遠，仍勒歸俗，其所犯罪重者，準格律處分。

translations.literal: If there are such persons, where they are shall strictly cut them off, escort to the border, and compel return to lay life; where crimes are heavy, punish according to the code.
translations.idiomatic: Offenders are to be arrested, exiled to the border, and forced back to lay life, with heavier crimes punished under law.

sentences.zh: 每年造僧帳兩本，其一本奏聞，一本申祠部，逐年四月十五日後，勒諸縣取索管界寺院僧尼數目申州，州司攢帳，至五月終已前文帳到京，僧尼籍帳內無名者，並勒還俗。

translations.literal: Each year two monk registers shall be made—one memorialized, one sent to the Ministry of Rites; after the fifteenth day of the fourth month each year the counties shall seek and report the numbers of monastery monks and nuns in their jurisdiction to the prefecture, the prefecture compile the register, and by the end of the fifth month the prior register must reach the capital; those not on the monk and nun rolls shall be compelled to return to lay life.
translations.idiomatic: Annual duplicate monk registers go to the throne and Ministry of Rites; counties report clergy by late spring, and anyone not registered is defrocked.

sentences.zh: 其巡禮行腳，出入往來，一切取便。

translations.literal: Itinerant pilgrimage and travel in and out are all permitted as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Pilgrimage and travel remain unrestricted.

sentences.zh: 是歲，諸道供到帳籍，所存寺院凡二千六百九十四所，廢寺院凡三萬三百三十六，僧尼系籍者六萬一千二百人。

translations.literal: This year registers submitted from the circuits showed monasteries remaining: 2,694; monasteries abolished: 30,336; monks and nuns on the rolls: 61,200.
translations.idiomatic: That year circuit registers recorded 2,694 monasteries retained, 30,336 abolished, and 61,200 registered monks and nuns.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以刑部侍郎邊光範為戶部侍郎，以前御史中丞裴巽為刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Vice Minister of Punishments Bian Guangfan was made Vice Minister of Revenue; former Censor-in-Chief Pei Xun was made Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Bian Guangfan moved from vice minister of punishments to vice minister of revenue, and Pei Xun from censor-in-chief to vice minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 己卯，刑部員外郎陳渥賜死，坐檢齊州臨邑縣民田失實也。

translations.literal: On jimao, Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments Chen Wo was sentenced to death for investigating the farmland of the people of Linyi County in Qizhou and finding it not factual.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Chen Wo, vice director of the ministry of punishments, was executed for falsifying his survey of peasant fields in Linyi, Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 渥為人清苦，臨事有守，以微累而當極刑，時論惜之。

translations.literal: Wo was a man of clean hardship; in affairs he had integrity—yet for a slight fault he received extreme punishment, and contemporary opinion mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wo lived plainly and acted with integrity, yet a minor fault brought capital punishment, to the regret of contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以沙州留後曹元忠為沙州節度使、檢校太尉、同平章事。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Acting Prefect of Shazhou Cao Yuanzhong was made Military Commissioner of Shazhou, Acting Grand Preceptor, and Fellow of the Secretariat with the Peaceful Registry.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Cao Yuanzhong, acting prefect of Shazhou, was made military commissioner of Shazhou, acting grand preceptor, and fellow of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丙申，禮部侍郎竇儀奏，請廢童子、明經二科及條貫考試次第，從之。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Vice Minister of Rites Dou Yi memorialized requesting abolition of the Child Prodigy and Mingjing examination categories and regulations on examination order; it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Dou Yi petitioned to abolish the child-prodigy and classics-memorization examinations and to revise grading rules; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 六月己酉，以曹州節度使韓通充西南面行營都虞候。

translations.literal: On jiyou in the sixth month, Caozhou Military Commissioner Han Tong was made Chief Controller of the Southwest Campaign Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Han Tong, military commissioner of Cao, was appointed chief controller of the southwestern campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以亳州防禦使陳思讓為邢州留後。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Bozhou Defense Commissioner Chen Siyang was made acting prefect of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Chen Siyang, defense commissioner of Bo, was made acting prefect of Xing.

sentences.zh: 庚申，詔：「兩京及諸道府州，不得奏薦留守判官、兩使判官、少尹、防禦團練軍事判官，如是隨幕已曾任此職者聽奏。

translations.literal: On gengshen, an edict: "The two capitals and all circuit prefectures must not memorialize recommending acting prefects, commissioners' aides, deputy prefects, or defense and militia military aides; if already holding such posts while on staff, memorializing is permitted.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen an edict barred recommending certain acting and staff posts from the two capitals and circuits, except for those already serving in such roles on a commissioner's staff.

sentences.zh: 防禦團練刺史州，各置推官一員。

translations.literal: Defense and militia prefectures shall each have one investigating official.
translations.idiomatic: Each defense or militia prefecture was to have one investigating official.

sentences.zh: 」辛酉，廢景州為定遠軍。

translations.literal: " On xinyou, Jingzhou was abolished and made Dingyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Jing Prefecture was abolished and redesignated Dingyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以前延州節度使袁鳷為滄州節度使，以前邢州節度使田景鹹為鄧州節度使。

translations.literal: On guihai, former Yanzhou Military Commissioner Yuan Zhi was made Cangzhou Military Commissioner; former Xingzhou Military Commissioner Tian Jingxian was made Dengzhou Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Yuan Zhi became military commissioner of Cang and Tian Jingxian of Deng.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丁卯朔，以鳳翔節度使王景兼西南面行營都招討使，以宣徽南院使、鎮安軍節度使向訓兼西南面行營都監。

translations.literal: On the first day of the seventh month, dingmao, Fengxiang Military Commissioner Wang Jing was additionally made Commander-in-Chief of the Southwest Campaign; Xuanhui Southern Court Commissioner and Zhen'an Military Commissioner Xiang Xun was additionally made Inspector-General of the Southwest Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On the autumn new moon Wang Jing of Fengxiang was named commander-in-chief of the southwestern campaign and Xiang Xun inspector-general.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，太子太傅、魯國公和凝卒。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Duke of Lu He Ning died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen He Ning, grand mentor of the heir apparent and duke of Lu, died.

sentences.zh: 八月癸卯，兵部尚書張昭、太常卿田敏等奏，議減祠祭所用犧牲之數，由是圜丘、方澤及太廟即用太牢，餘皆以羊代之。

translations.literal: On guimao in the eighth month, Minister of War Zhang Zhao, Director of Court Music Tian Min, and others memorialized on reducing the number of sacrificial animals used in state worship; thereafter the Round Mound, Square Mound, and Grand Temple used the great offering, while the rest were replaced with sheep.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Zhang Zhao and Tian Min proposed cutting sacrificial livestock; thereafter the grand temples used the full ox offering and lesser rites used sheep.

sentences.zh: 丁未，中書侍郎、平章事、判三司景範罷判三司，加銀青光祿大夫，依前中書侍郎、平章事，進封開國伯；

translations.literal: On dingwei, Secretariat Vice Director, Grand Councillor, and Commissioner of the Three Departments Jing Fan was removed from the Three Departments, advanced to Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, remaining Secretariat Vice Director and Grand Councillor, and enfeoffed as Baron of the State;
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Jing Fan left the Three Departments commission, kept his grand councillor rank, and was enfeoffed a baron;

sentences.zh: 以樞密院承旨張美權判三司。

translations.literal: Pivot Court Academician-in-Attendance Zhang Mei was made acting commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mei, pivot court academician-in-attendance, was made acting commissioner of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，詔：「今後應有病患老弱馬，並送同州沙苑監、衛州牧馬監，就彼水草，以盡飲龁之性。

translations.literal: On xinhai, an edict: "Hereafter sick, old, and weak horses shall all be sent to Tongzhou Shayuan Pasturage and Weizhou Horse Pasturage; there with water and grass their nature of drinking and grazing may be fully satisfied."
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai an edict ordered sick and aged horses sent to pasturages at Tong and Wei to recover on pasture.

sentences.zh: 」庚子，太子太師致仕趙暉卒。

translations.literal: " On gengzi, Retired Grand Preceptor Zhao Hui died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the retired grand preceptor Zhao Hui died.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，詔曰：「今後諸處祠祭，應有牲牢、香幣、饌料、供具等，仰委本司官吏躬親檢校，務在精至。

translations.literal: On yichou, an edict stated: "Hereafter at sacrifices everywhere, sacrificial animals, incense, coins, food offerings, and vessels shall be personally inspected by officials of the responsible office, with utmost care for refinement.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou an edict required local officials to inspect sacrificial supplies personally and follow the Rites in ceremony.

sentences.zh: 行事儀式，依附《禮經》，大祠祭合用樂者，仍須祀前教習。

translations.literal: Ritual procedures shall follow the Book of Rites; where great sacrifices require music, rehearsal is still required before the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Major rites were to follow the Book of Rites, with music rehearsed beforehand.

sentences.zh: 凡關祀事，宜令太常博士及監察御史用心點檢，稍或因循，必行朝典。」

translations.literal: All matters relating to sacrifice should be carefully checked by Court of Imperial Sacrifices erudites and investigating censors; the slightest perfunctoriness will bring court punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Erudites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and investigating censors were to scrutinize all rites; negligence would bring disciplinary action.

sentences.zh: 九月丙寅朔，詔禁天下銅器，始議立監鑄錢。

translations.literal: On the first day of the ninth month, bingyin, an edict forbade bronze vessels throughout the realm and began discussion of establishing a mint to cast coin.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth-month new moon bronze vessels were banned empire-wide and a state mint was proposed.

sentences.zh: 癸未，以太子賓客趙上交為吏部侍郎，以吏部侍郎於德辰、司徒詡並為太子賓客。

translations.literal: On guawei, Heir Apparent Tutor Zhao Shangjiao was made Vice Minister of Personnel; Vice Ministers of Personnel Yu Dechen and Situ Xu were both made Heir Apparent Tutors.
translations.idiomatic: On guawei Zhao Shangjiao became vice minister of personnel and Yu Dechen and Situ Xu heir-apparent tutors.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，詔文武百僚，今後遇天清節，依近臣例各賜衣服。

translations.literal: On yiyou, an edict ordered all civil and military officials that hereafter on the Tianqing Festival each should receive garments as the close ministers do.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou civil and military officials were granted festival garments like those given close ministers.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，西南面招討使王景，部送所獲西川軍校姜暉已下三百人至闕。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Southwest Commander Wang Jing escorted captured Former Shu military officers including Jiang Hui and three hundred men below to the court.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Wang Jing delivered more than three hundred captured Shu officers, including Jiang Hui, to the capital.

sentences.zh: 甲午，潞州部送先擒到河東兵馬監押程支等二百人至闕。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Luzhou escorted previously captured Hedong army supervisor Cheng Zhi and two hundred men to the court.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Luzhou delivered two hundred captured Hedong troops led by Cheng Zhi.

sentences.zh: 詔所獲西川、河東軍校已下並釋之，各賜錢帛有差。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all captured Shu and Hedong military officers below released and each given money and silks in differing amounts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered all such captives released and given cash and silks in graded amounts.

sentences.zh: 閏月壬子，西南面招討使王景奏，大破西川賊軍於黃花谷，擒偽命都監王巒、孫韜等一千五百餘人。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month on renzi, Southwest Commander Wang Jing memorialized a great defeat of Shu rebels at Huanghua Valley, capturing the false-appointment overseer Wang Luan, Sun Tao, and more than 1,500 men.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month Wang Jing reported crushing Shu forces at Huanghua Valley and capturing Wang Luan, Sun Tao, and over 1,500 men.

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·李廷珪傳》：周師攻秦、鳳，以廷珪為北路行營都統，高彥儔、呂彥珂為招討。

translations.literal: (Jiuguo Zhi, biography of Li Tinggui: Zhou armies attacked Qin and Feng; Tinggui was made overall commander of the northern route, Gao Yanshou and Lü Yanke recruiters.
translations.idiomatic: (Jiuguo Zhi, Li Tinggui: When Zhou attacked Qin and Feng, Li Tinggui commanded the northern route with Gao Yanshou and Lü Yanke as recruiters.

sentences.zh: 廷珪遣先鋒指揮使李進以兵據馬嶺，分兵出斜谷，營於白澗，將腹背以攻周師；

translations.literal: Tinggui sent vanguard commander Li Jin with troops to hold Maling, divided troops out of Xiegu, and camped at Baixian, intending to attack the Zhou army front and rear;
translations.idiomatic: Li Tinggui sent Li Jin to hold Maling, detached troops through Xiegu, and camped at Baixian to pinch the Zhou force;

sentences.zh: 又遣染院使王巒領兵出唐倉，與周師遇，蜀師敗走，王巒死之。

translations.literal: also sent Dye-House Commissioner Wang Luan with troops out of Tangcang; meeting the Zhou army, Shu troops were defeated and fled, and Wang Luan died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Luan led troops from Tangcang, met Zhou forces, was defeated, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 而馬嶺、斜谷之兵聞之皆退奔，高彥儔與諸將謀退守青泥嶺。

translations.literal: When troops at Maling and Xiegu heard this they all fled; Gao Yanshou and the generals planned to retreat to Qingni Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Troops at Maling and Xiegu fled on the news, and Gao Yanshou planned a retreat to Qingni Ridge.

sentences.zh: 由是秦、鳳、階、成之地，皆陷於周矣。）〉

translations.literal: Thereby the lands of Qin, Feng, Jie, and Cheng all fell to Zhou.)]
translations.idiomatic: Qin, Feng, Jie, and Cheng then all fell to Zhou.)]

sentences.zh: 癸丑，秦州偽命觀察判官趙比以本城降，詔以比為郢州刺史。

translations.literal: On guichou, Qinzhou false-appointment observer and judge Zhao Bi surrendered the city; an edict made Bi Prefect of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Zhao Bi, Shu's observer at Qin, surrendered the city and was made prefect of Ying.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·趙比傳》：高彥儔出師救援，未至，聞軍敗，因潰歸。

translations.literal: (Song Shi, biography of Zhao Bi: Gao Yanshou marched to rescue; before arriving he heard of defeat and fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: (Song Shi, Zhao Bi: Gao Yanshou marched to relieve the city but fled on hearing of defeat.

sentences.zh: 比閉門不納，召官屬諭之曰：「今中朝兵甲無敵於天下，自用師西征，戰無不勝，蜀中所遣將皆武勇者，卒皆驍健者，然殺戮遁逃之外，幾無孑遺。

translations.literal: Bi closed the gates and would not admit him, summoned officials and told them: "Now the central court's arms and armor are unmatched in the realm; since they campaigned west, they have been undefeated. The generals Shu sent were all martially brave and their soldiers all fierce and strong—yet apart from slaughter and flight, scarcely one survivor remains.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bi shut him out and told his staff that Zhou armies were invincible and Shu armies had been nearly annihilated.

sentences.zh: 我輩安忍坐受其禍，去危就安，當在今日。

translations.literal: How can we bear to sit and receive this calamity? Leaving danger for safety should be today."
translations.idiomatic: He asked how they could endure the coming disaster and urged surrender that day.

sentences.zh: 」眾皆俯伏聽命，比遂以城歸順。

translations.literal: All bowed and listened to orders; Bi then surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: All assented and he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 世宗欲命以藩鎮，宰相範質不可，乃授郢州刺史。）〉

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to appoint him to a military commission; Chief Councillor Fan Zhi objected, and he was made only Prefect of Ying.)]
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to give him a frontier command, but Fan Zhi objected, and he received only Ying prefecture.)]

sentences.zh: 先是，帝以西師久次，艱於糧運，命今上乘驛赴軍前，以觀攻戰之勢。

translations.literal: Earlier the Emperor, because the western army was long encamped and grain transport difficult, ordered the heir apparent to take post relays to the front to observe the trend of attack.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, with the western campaign stalled by supply problems, the emperor had sent the heir apparent by relay post to observe operations.

sentences.zh: 及回，具以事勢上奏，帝甚悅，至是果成功焉。

translations.literal: On return he fully memorialized the situation; the Emperor was very pleased—at this time success was indeed achieved.
translations.idiomatic: His report pleased the emperor, and success now followed as he had foretold.

sentences.zh: 甲子，秘書少監許遜責授蔡州別駕，坐先假竇氏圖書隱而不還也。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Vice Director of the Secretariat Xu Xun was demoted to Vice Prefect of Cai, sitting because he had earlier borrowed Dou clan books and concealed them without returning.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Xu Xun was demoted to vice prefect of Cai for keeping borrowed books from the Dou clan.

sentences.zh: 冬十月庚午，召近臣射於苑中，賜金器鞍馬有差。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on gengwu, close ministers were summoned to shoot in the park and given gold vessels, saddles, and horses in differing amounts.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the emperor summoned close ministers to archery in the imperial park and bestowed gold vessels, saddles, and horses.

sentences.zh: 辛未，成州歸順。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Chengzhou submitted allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Cheng Prefecture surrendered.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，以給事中王敏為工部侍郎。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Attendant-in-Waiting Wang Min was made Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou Wang Min, attendant-in-waiting, was made vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，高麗國遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Goryeo sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Goryeo presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，右散騎常侍康澄責授環州別駕，左司郎中史又元責授商州長史，左驍衛大將軍元霸責授均州別駕，右驍衛將軍林延禔責授登州長史。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Right Regular Attendant Kang Cheng was demoted to Vice Prefect of Huan; Left Bureau Director Shi Youyuan to Senior Administrator of Shang; Left Brave Guard Grand General Yuan Ba to Vice Prefect of Jun; Right Brave Guard General Lin Yanti to Senior Administrator of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou several envoys were demoted for lingering privately in Zhe while on mission.

sentences.zh: 澄等奉使浙中，回日以私便停留，逾時復命，故有是責。

translations.literal: Cheng and others, on returning from mission to Zhe, stayed for private convenience and exceeded time in reporting—therefore this punishment.
translations.idiomatic: They had delayed their return from the lower Yangzi region for private reasons.

sentences.zh: 右諫議大夫李知損配流沙門島，坐妄貢章疏，斥讟貴近，及求使兩浙故也。

translations.literal: Right Remonstrance Officer Li Zhisun was assigned to Liushamen Island, sitting because he rashly submitted memorials slandering the honored and near and because he sought mission to the two Zhe regions.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhisun was exiled to Liushamen Island for abusive memorials and seeking a Zhe mission.

sentences.zh: 己丑，前太常卿邊蔚卒。

translations.literal: On jichou, former Director of Court Music Bian Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the former director of court music Bian Wei died.

sentences.zh: 是月始議南征。

translations.literal: This month discussion of a southern campaign began.
translations.idiomatic: That month the court began planning the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙未朔，以宰臣李穀為淮南道前軍行營都部署，知廬、壽等州行府事；

translations.literal: On the first day of the eleventh month, yiwei, Chief Councillor Li Gu was made Overall Commander of the Huainan Forward Army Headquarters, knowing the affairs of the campaign office of Lu and Shou prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh-month new moon Li Gu was named overall commander of the Huainan forward headquarters for Lu and Shou;

sentences.zh: 以許州節度使王彥超為行營副部署；

translations.literal: Xuzhou Military Commissioner Wang Yanchao was made Deputy Commander of the Headquarters;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanchao of Xu was made his deputy;

sentences.zh: 命侍衛馬軍都指揮使韓令坤等一十二將，各帶征行之號以從焉。

translations.literal: the Palace Guard Horse Army Commander Han Lingkun and twelve other generals were ordered, each bearing an expeditionary title, to follow.
translations.idiomatic: and Han Lingkun and eleven other generals were ordered to follow with expeditionary titles.

sentences.zh: 己亥，諭淮南州縣，詔曰：

translations.literal: On jihai, Huainan prefectures and counties were instructed; the edict stated:
translations.idiomatic: On jihai the court addressed Huainan prefectures and counties:

sentences.zh: 朕自纘承基構，統御寰瀛，方當恭己臨朝，誕修文德，豈欲興兵動眾，專耀武功！

translations.literal: We have succeeded to the foundation and rule the realm; we ought to be respectful and restrained in court, broadly cultivating civil virtue—how could We wish to raise troops and move the masses, solely to display martial achievement!
translations.idiomatic: Having inherited the throne, I ought to govern through civil virtue rather than boast of arms,

sentences.zh: 顧茲昏亂之邦，須舉吊伐之義。

translations.literal: But looking at this benighted and disorderly region, We must raise the righteous army of consolation and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: yet this rebellious region compels a punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 蠢爾淮甸，敢拒大幫，因唐室之陵遲，接黃寇之紛亂，飛揚跋扈，垂六十年，盜據一方，僭稱偽號。

translations.literal: You reckless Huai region dare resist the great state; taking advantage of the Tang house's decline you joined the Yellow Bandits' turmoil, arrogant and overbearing for nearly sixty years, stealing a territory and falsely assuming a title.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai lords have defied the throne for sixty years, seizing territory and assuming a false imperial title amid Tang's decline and bandit chaos.

sentences.zh: 幸數朝之多事，與北境以交通，厚啟兵端，誘為邊患。

translations.literal: Fortunately for the many troubles of several reigns, you trafficked with the northern border, thickly opening military quarrels and luring border calamity.
translations.idiomatic: They trafficked with northern enemies and provoked frontier wars through successive dynasties.

sentences.zh: 晉、漢之代，寰海未寧，而乃招納叛亡，朋助兇慝，李金全之據安陸，李守貞之叛河中，大起師徒，來為應援，攻侵高密，殺掠吏民，迫奪閩、越之封疆，塗炭湘、潭之士庶。

translations.literal: In the Jin and Han eras the realm was not at peace, yet you recruited fugitive rebels and aided vicious criminals—Li Jinquan holding Anlu, Li Shouzhen rebelling at Hezhong—you raised great armies in support, attacked Gaomi, slaughtered officials and people, seized Min and Yue frontiers, and ravaged Xiang and Tan commoners.
translations.idiomatic: They sheltered rebels such as Li Jinquan and Li Shouzhen, raided Shandong, and ravaged Fujian, Hunan, and nearby regions.

sentences.zh: 以至我朝啟運，東魯不庭，發兵而應接叛臣，觀釁而憑淩徐部。

translations.literal: Down to Our dynasty's founding, the eastern Lu did not attend court; you sent troops supporting rebel ministers and watched for chances to bully Xu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At our founding they aided Shandong rebels and harassed Xu.

sentences.zh: 沭陽之役，曲直可知，尚示包荒，猶稽問罪。

translations.literal: At the battle of Shuyang right and wrong were clear; We still showed forbearance and delayed punishment.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuyang they were shown forbearance though guilt was clear.

sentences.zh: 邇後維揚一境，連歲阻饑，我國家念彼災荒，大許糴易。

translations.literal: Recently in Yangzhou one circuit suffered famine year after year; Our state, pitying that disaster, greatly permitted grain sales.
translations.idiomatic: We even sold them grain when Yangzhou starved.

sentences.zh: 前後擒獲將士，皆遣放還，自來禁戢邊兵，不令侵撓。

translations.literal: Captured officers and men before and after were all sent home; from the first Our border troops were forbidden to harass.
translations.idiomatic: Captured soldiers were released and border troops restrained.

sentences.zh: 我無所負，彼實多奸，勾誘契丹至今未已，結連並寇與我為讎，罪惡難名，人神共憤。

translations.literal: We have owed them nothing; they have been truly treacherous, enticing Khitan down to today without cease, joining with Bing enemies as Our foes—crime hard to name, men and spirits together enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they kept enticing Khitans and Bing foes and remain our enemies, outraging heaven and man.

sentences.zh: 今則推輪命將，鳴鼓出師，征浙右之樓船，下朗陵之戈甲，東西合勢，水陸齊攻。

translations.literal: Now We deploy commanders and sound the drums of expedition, summoning warships of the Zhe right and lowering spears and armor of Langling—east and west combining force, water and land attacking together.
translations.idiomatic: Now armies advance by land and water from east and west.

sentences.zh: 吳孫皓之計窮，自當歸命；

translations.literal: When Wu's Sun Hao's plans were exhausted, he naturally submitted;
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Hao's schemes failed he submitted;

sentences.zh: 陳叔寶之數盡，何處偷生！

translations.literal: when Chen Shubao's fate was spent, where could he steal life!
translations.idiomatic: when Chen Shubao's luck ran out he could not escape!

sentences.zh: 應淮南將士軍人百姓等，久隔朝廷，莫聞聲教，雖從偽俗，應樂華風，必須善擇安危，早圖去就。

translations.literal: All Huainan officers, soldiers, and commoners long cut off from court and hearing Our civilizing teaching—though following false customs, they should delight in Chinese style; they must choose safety and danger early and decide to leave or stay.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan soldiers and people should choose safety and return to imperial rule.

sentences.zh: 如能投戈獻款，舉郡來降，具牛酒以犒師，納圭符而請命，車服玉帛豈吝旌酬，土地山河誠無愛惜。

translations.literal: If they cast weapons and offer allegiance, surrendering whole commanderies, presenting ox and wine to reward the army and submitting seals to request orders—carriages, robes, jade, and silks will not be stinted in reward, and land and mountains are truly without stinginess.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendering districts with gifts and seals will be richly rewarded with titles and land.

sentences.zh: 刑賞之令，信若丹青，茍或執迷，寧免後悔。

translations.literal: Orders of punishment and reward are trustworthy as black and red; if stubbornly deluded, how can they avoid later regret.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and punishments are certain; obstinacy will bring regret.

sentences.zh: 王師所至，軍政甚明，不犯秋毫，有如時雨，百姓父老各務安居，剽擄焚燒必令禁止雲。

translations.literal: Where Our army arrives, military government is very clear, not violating a hair, like timely rain; elders and commoners should each seek peaceful dwelling, and plunder and burning are surely forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Our troops will be disciplined as timely rain and forbid looting and burning.

sentences.zh: 高麗國王王昭加開府儀同三司、檢校太尉，依前使持節元菟州都督、大義軍使，王如故。

translations.literal: Goryeo King Wang Zhao was made Grand Master of the Palace with the same registry as before, still bearing the staff as Commander-in-Chief of Wonju and Commissioner of the Great Righteous Army; the king as before.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo's Wang Zhao was advanced in rank while retaining his titles.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以前滄州節度使李暉為邠州節度使。

translations.literal: On xinhai, former Cangzhou Military Commissioner Li Hui was made Binzhou Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Li Hui was transferred from Cang to Bin.

sentences.zh: 壬子，潞州奏，破河東賊軍於祁縣。

translations.literal: On renzi, Luzhou memorialized breaking Hedong rebel armies at Qi County.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Luzhou reported victory over Hedong rebels at Qi.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，西南面行營都部署王景奏，收復鳳州，獲偽命節度使王環。

translations.literal: On guichou, Southwest Commander Wang Jing memorialized recovering Fengzhou and capturing false-appointment Military Commissioner Wang Huan.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Wang Jing recovered Feng and captured Wang Huan.

sentences.zh: 乙卯。

translations.literal: On yimao.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao.

sentences.zh: 曲赦秦、鳳、階、成等州管內罪人，自顯德二年十一月已前，凡有罪犯，無問輕重，一切釋放。

translations.literal: A partial amnesty for criminals within Qin, Feng, Jie, and Cheng prefectures: from before the eleventh month of Xiande 2, all crimes regardless of severity were released.
translations.idiomatic: A partial amnesty was declared for Qin, Feng, Jie, and Cheng for all crimes before the eleventh month of Xiande 2.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，前邠州節度使折從阮卒。

translations.literal: On dingsi, former Binzhou Military Commissioner Zhe Congruan died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Zhe Congruan, former commissioner of Bin, died.

sentences.zh: 己未，邢州奏，河東劉崇死。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Xingzhou memorialized that Hedong's Liu Chong died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Xing reported the death of Liu Chong of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，淮南前軍都部署李穀奏，先鋒都指揮使白延遇破淮賊於來遠鎮。

translations.literal: On renxu, Huainan Forward Commander Li Gu memorialized Vanguard Commander Bai Yanyu defeating Huai rebels at Laiyuan Town.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Li Gu reported Bai Yanyu's victory over Huai rebels at Laiyuan.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙寅，以左金吾大將軍蓋萬為右監門上將軍。

translations.literal: On bingyin in the twelfth month, Left Golden Crow General Gai Wan was made Right Gate Senior General.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Gai Wan was made senior general of the right gate.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，淄州奏，前中書侍郎、同平章事景範卒。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Zizhou memorialized that former Secretariat Vice Director and Grand Councillor Jing Fan died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Zizhou reported the death of Jing Fan.

sentences.zh: 庚午，右金吾衛上將軍王守恩卒。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Right Golden Crow Guard Senior General Wang Shou'en died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Wang Shou'en died.

sentences.zh: 辛未，安州奏，盜殺防禦使張穎。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Anzhou memorialized that bandits killed Defense Commissioner Zhang Ying.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei An reported that bandits had killed Zhang Ying, defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是日，翰林學士承旨徐臺符卒。

translations.literal: That day, Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance Xu Taifu died.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Xu Taifu, Hanlin academician-in-attendance, died.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，李穀奏，破淮賊二千人於壽州城下。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Li Gu memorialized defeating two thousand Huai rebels below Shouzhou city.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Li Gu defeated two thousand Huai rebels below Shou.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以左諫議大夫、權知開封府事王樸為左散騎常侍，充端明殿學士，依前權知開封府事。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Left Remonstrance Officer and Acting Mayor of Kaifeng Wang Pu was made Left Regular Attendant, made Duanming Hall Academician, and continued as Acting Mayor of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Wang Pu was made regular attendant and Duanming academician while keeping acting mayor of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 永興軍奏，節度使劉詞卒。

translations.literal: Yongxing Army memorialized that Military Commissioner Liu Ci died.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing reported the death of Liu Ci, its military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 己卯，李穀奏，破淮賊千餘人於山口鎮。

translations.literal: On jimao, Li Gu memorialized defeating more than a thousand Huai rebels at Shankou Town.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Li Gu defeated over a thousand Huai rebels at Shankou.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，樞密使鄭仁誨卒。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Pivot Commissioner Zheng Renhui died.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Zheng Renhui, pivot commissioner, died.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，西南面行營都部署王景，差人部送所獲偽鳳翔節度使王環至闕。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Southwest Commander Wang Jing sent men escorting the captured false Fengxiang Military Commissioner Wang Huan to the court.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Wang Jing sent the captured Wang Huan of Fengxiang to the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔釋之，仍賜鞍馬衣服，尋授右驍衛

translations.literal: An edict released him and still bestowed saddle, horse, and clothes; soon he was appointed Right Brave Guard
translations.idiomatic: An edict freed him, gave him saddle, horse, and robes, and soon appointed him to the Right Brave Guard

sentences.zh: 大將軍。

translations.literal: Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General.

sentences.zh: 是冬，命起居郎陶文舉征殘租於宋州。

translations.literal: That winter, Court Diarist Tao Wengu was ordered to collect arrears of rent at Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Tao Wengu, court diarist, was sent to collect overdue rent at Song.

sentences.zh: 文舉本酷吏也，宋民被其刑者凡數千，冤號之聲聞於道路，有悼髦之輩，不勝其刑而死者數人，物議以為不允。

translations.literal: Wengu was originally a harsh official; Song commoners who suffered his punishments numbered several thousand—the sound of wrongful cries was heard on the roads; there were youths in mourning who could not bear his punishments and several died; public opinion held it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Wengu was a notorious harsh official; thousands in Song suffered under him, wails filled the roads, several died under torture, and public opinion condemned the mission.
